n: A new message from the Lord to Jeremiah, this time about the covenant.

Hear the words of “this covenant” and tell them to Judah and Jerusalem. Many scholars think this refers to the covenant renewed under Josiah after the Book of the Law (likely Deuteronomy) was found in the temple.

f.w: this covenant

n: Cursed is anyone who doesn’t obey the terms of this covenant. The covenant included blessings for obedience and curses for disobedience.

f.w: Cursed be the man that obeyeth not

n: God gave this covenant when He brought Israel out of Egypt—the “iron furnace” of slavery. The heart of it: obey My voice, and you will be My people and I will be your God.

f.w: the iron furnace
f.g: A smelting furnace—an image of Egypt’s harsh bondage.

f.w: so shall ye be my people, and I will be your God

n: Obedience allowed God to keep His oath to give them a land flowing with milk and honey. Jeremiah answers, “Amen, Lord”—he agrees with God’s terms.

f.w: a land flowing with milk and honey
So be it
f.g: Hebrew amen—“truly, let it be so.”

n: God sends Jeremiah through Judah’s towns and Jerusalem’s streets: listen to the covenant and live by it.

f.w: Hear ye the words of this covenant, and do them

n: Ever since the Exodus God warned their ancestors persistently—rising early to warn them—“Obey My voice.”

f.w: rising early and protesting

n: But they didn’t obey; each followed his stubborn heart. So God brought on them all the covenant’s curses.

f.w: the imagination of their evil heart

n: God reveals a conspiracy in Judah and Jerusalem—a deliberate, organized turning away from Him.

f.w: A conspiracy

n: They have gone back to their ancestors’ sins and other gods. Both Israel and Judah have broken the covenant. Josiah’s reforms were apparently being undone.

f.w: have broken my covenant

n: So God will bring a disaster they can’t escape, and though they cry to Him, He won’t listen.

f.w: though they shall cry unto me, I will not hearken

n: Then they’ll run to the gods they burned incense to—but those gods won’t save them at all.

f.w: they shall not save them at all

n: Judah has as many gods as towns and as many Baal altars as Jerusalem has streets. Baal is called “that shameful thing.”

f.w: according to the number of thy cities were thy gods
that shameful thing
f.g: Hebrew boshet, a scornful substitute for Baal’s name.

n: So again: don’t pray for this people—God won’t listen when they cry out in trouble.

f.w: pray not thou for this people

n: What right does My beloved have in My house when she has done so many vile deeds? Can sacred meat (sacrifices) take away your sin? You even celebrate when you do evil.

f.w: my beloved
the holy flesh
f.g: Sacrificial meat; the Hebrew may ask, “Can vows and holy meat remove your evil?”

n: The Lord once called Israel a flourishing olive tree, beautiful with good fruit. Now, with a roar like a storm, He sets it on fire and its branches break. Compare Zenos’s allegory of Israel as an olive tree.

f.w: A green olive tree

n: The Lord who planted Israel has decreed disaster because of the evil they did, provoking Him by burning incense to Baal. They brought it on themselves.

f.w: which they have done against themselves

n: A new section: God reveals to Jeremiah a plot against his life.

Jeremiah was like a trusting lamb led to slaughter, not knowing they were plotting: “Let’s destroy the tree with its fruit and wipe his name from memory.” The language anticipates Isaiah 53 and Jesus’s rejection.

f.w: like a lamb or an ox that is brought to the slaughter
cut him off from the land of the living

n: Jeremiah appeals to God, who judges fairly and tests the deepest thoughts and heart: let me see You act against them, for I’ve committed my case to You.

f.w: triest the reins and the heart
f.g: Reins = kidneys, thought of as the seat of emotions; God examines inner feelings and thoughts.

n: The plotters were men from Anathoth—Jeremiah’s own hometown and probably relatives—who threatened, “Stop prophesying in the Lord’s name or we’ll kill you.”

f.w: the men of Anathoth
Prophesy not in the name of the LORD

n: God promises to punish them: young men will die by the sword and their children by famine.

No remnant of the plotters will be left when their time of punishment comes. Interestingly, Ezra 2:23 records 128 men of Anathoth returning from exile—the town survived, though the conspirators didn’t.

f.w: the year of their visitation
there shall be no remnant of them
